newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Jan 1-29 trade deficit seen at $4.1 bln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Jan 1-29 trade deficit seen at $4.1 bln.

text.p: South Korea's customs-cleared trade deficit during the first 29 days of January was estimated at $4.1 billion, Finance Minister Han Seung-soo said on Friday.
The deficit, the biggest monthly figure ever, compares with a shortfall of $2.13 billion for the whole of January 1996.

Han told a meeting of economy ministers that exports during the 29-day period were estimated at $7.6 billion, down 10.2 percent from a year earlier, while imports rose 5.4 percent to $11.7 billion. He said exports were hampered by strikes that hit the nation's auto industry and falling semiconductor prices.
The strikes in protest at passage of a controversial labour law had crippled much of South Korean industries between December 26 and January 18.
In 1996, South Korea's trade deficit totalled a record $20.38 billion, against a $10.06 billion shortfall in 1995.
